description: SentryPrompt4 detection categories and rule patterns (NFR-005). Categories are listed in priority order: when matches from two rule-based categories overlap, the one listed first wins. Descriptions are shown to students as plain-language explanations (FR-006, NFR-001).

categories.name: SA_ID
categories.description: This looks like a South African ID number. An ID number identifies you personally and can be used for identity fraud, so it should not be shared with an AI tool.

categories.name: BANK_CARD
categories.description: This looks like a bank card number. Card numbers can be used to make payments in your name, so never share them with an AI tool.

patterns.description: 13–19 digit card number, optionally grouped with spaces or dashes; must pass the Luhn checksum

categories.name: BANK_ACCOUNT
categories.description: This looks like a bank or loan account number. Account numbers are financial information that could be misused, so leave them out of your prompt.

patterns.description: 8–12 digit number directly after the word 'account' (or acc/acct)

categories.name: PHONE
categories.description: This looks like a phone number. A phone number lets someone contact or identify you directly, so it is personal information.

patterns.description: South African mobile number (+27, 27 or 0 prefix); the lookbehind keeps a leading '+' inside the match

categories.name: EMAIL
categories.description: This looks like an email address. Email addresses are personal contact details and can identify you, so avoid including them.

patterns.description: Email address (lengths bounded to email limits to prevent ReDoS)

categories.name: ADDRESS
categories.description: This looks like a street address. Where you live is personal location information, so it should not be shared with an AI tool.

patterns.description: House number, up to six capitalised words, and a street type

categories.name: STUDENT_NUMBER
categories.description: This looks like a student number. Your student number identifies you at your university, so it counts as personal information.

patterns.description: 7–9 digit student number, optionally after 'stu' or 'student'

categories.name: MEDICAL
categories.description: This mentions health information, such as a diagnosis, medication or mental health. Health details are especially sensitive personal information under POPIA, so consider leaving them out or describing your situation more generally.

categories.name: INSTITUTIONAL
categories.description: This mentions confidential university information, such as disciplinary matters, someone else's results or unpublished exam content. Sharing it could breach university policy or another person's privacy.
